title: Objective-to-Initiative Allocation & Escalation Matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: produce a repeatable, operationalized mapping from company-level objectives to concrete initiative slices with a clear allocation of team capacity and an automated escalation trigger set. Deliverables: 1) a CSV matrix mapping OKRs -> initiative slices -> owners -> estimated capacity (FTE-weeks) -> risk score; 2) an escalation policy (soft and hard triggers) and a runbook for PM/Eng/Design when an initiative threatens the company-level objective; 3) a Linear workflow template that auto-tags blocked slices for leadership review; 4) a short Confluence guide for OKR owners to use during quarterly planning and rebalancing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Matrix CSV produced and validated by at least 3 cross-functional leads (PM, Eng, Design).
- Escalation policy accepted by GTM and Eng leads and added to incident playbooks.
- Linear template created and integrated into company roadmap board.
- Two simulated escalations run in tabletop exercise with documented adjustments.
notes: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff aligned with GTM and Eng. Agreed scope: focus on top 6 company objectives for Q1 and Q2 crosswalk. Asked ENG to provide capacity model exports by 2026-02-27.
2026-02-27 - Marco Li: Received raw capacity export from ENG-21456. Numbers require normalization for contractors and cross-functional time. Created initial allocation prototype (see drive link).

2026-03-03 - Design review (Elena Torres): Design input: initiative slices need clear customer signals and acceptance tests; recommended adding a 'regression delta' field to the matrix. Added to prototype.

2026-03-05 - Engineering feedback (Jonah Park): Raised a flag about kernel/serving runtime initiatives that span multiple teams. Proposed mapping those to a shared dependency token and adding a dependency column in Linear. Tagged ENG-21456 as primary dependency.

2026-03-08 - Leadership sync (VP PM + Head Eng): Approved escalation thresholds: soft at 40% overrun vs plan OR two-week lag on critical path; hard at 60% overrun OR four-week lag. Ownership: PM owner must file escalation; Eng SVP signs off on fallback allocations.

2026-03-10 - Action: Built Linear workflow template (PM-Template-OKR-Allocation) and tested creation of initiative slices. Auto-tag rule added: if a slice is marked 'blocked' AND estimated remaining work > 2 FTE-weeks, post a notification to #leadership-review.

2026-03-11 - Risk scoring iteration: Added three axes for risk (technical complexity, external dependency, quality/regression risk). Each axis 0-5; automated aggregate computed in CSV. Requested ENG to validate scoring heuristics in a follow-up workshop.
2026-03-12 - Next: Run tabletop escalation simulation on 2026-03-18 with PM, Eng leads, and Ops. Finalize Confluence guide after simulation.
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Add 'regression delta' column to track ML quality vs baseline for model-serving initiatives. Decision by Design and PM.
2026-03-08: Escalation thresholds set (soft: 40%/2 weeks; hard: 60%/4 weeks). Decision by VP PM and Head Eng.
2026-03-10: Linear template will auto-tag high-impact blocked slices to #leadership-review. Decision by PM tooling owners.
2026-03-11: Use 3-axis risk score (complexity, dependency, regression) aggregated by weighted sum (weights: 0.4/0.3/0.3). Decision by Eng and PM risk workshop.
next_steps: 1) Run tabletop simulation 2026-03-18 and capture play-by-play. 2) Iterate risk heuristics with Eng during 2026-03-20 workshop. 3) Publish Confluence guide and call out mandatory usage for all company OKR owners before roadmap freeze on 2026-03-31. 4) Deliver final CSV + Linear integration by 2026-04-01.
related_metrics: Target: reduce company OKR drift by 30% vs prior quarter (measured as percent of objectives with >2 week slippage). Secondary: reduce token-level cost overruns on prioritized initiatives by 20% via reallocation triggers.
communication_plan:

- Tabletop exercise observed by ops and recorded.
- Confluence guide published with a short Loom walkthrough.
- Post-mortem & improvements circulated via all-hands summary and product community channel.
